documents.title: ADR 0001: Adopt .NET 10 as Target Framework
documents.description: Mandates .NET 10 LTS as the target framework for all new projects, covering runtime choice rationale, upgrade cadence, and minimum language version expectations.

documents.title: ADR 0002: Central Package Management for .NET Solutions
documents.description: Adopts NuGet Central Package Management (CPM) with a root-level Directory.Packages.props to declare all package versions once, preventing version drift across a multi-project solution.

documents.title: ADR 0003: Strong Recommendation to Adopt .NET Aspire for ASP.NET Web Services
documents.description: Requires .NET Aspire for all web-enabled solutions. Covers AppHost/ServiceDefaults project naming under src/Aspire/, service registration, AddServiceDefaults(), and MapDefaultEndpoints() conventions.

documents.title: ADR 0004: Standardize Result Objects for Expected Application Outcomes
documents.description: Standardizes Result/Result<T> as the application-boundary contract for expected business outcomes, while reserving exceptions for unexpected technical failures.

documents.title: ADR 0005: Modular Monolith Project Structure
documents.description: Defines the canonical top-level solution layout: App/, Aspire/, Core/, per-domain module folders (each with module, Abstractions, Api, Data, Tests projects), and integration event contracts. The authoritative reference for where every project lives in the repository.

documents.title: ADR 0006: Recommendation to Implement CQRS for ASP.NET API Projects
documents.description: Adopts lightweight CQRS using custom ICommandHandler<TCommand, TResult> and IQueryHandler<TQuery, TResult> interfaces from the Core project. Explicitly rejects MediatR to avoid unnecessary indirection.

documents.title: ADR 0007: Recommend Minimal APIs Over Controller-Based APIs
documents.description: Mandates ASP.NET Core Minimal APIs with endpoint classes (not controllers). Covers MapGroup, endpoint naming, native ASP.NET 10 OpenAPI (AddOpenApi/MapOpenApi), Scalar as the API UI, shallow endpoint-filter validation, and how thin endpoints delegate to CQRS handlers.

documents.title: ADR 0008: Adopt Vertical Slice Architecture for Feature Organization
documents.description: Requires organizing features as vertical slices: each use case gets its own folder with command/query, handler, and endpoint filter for shallow validation. DTOs go in the .Abstractions project (DataTransferObjects/); domain model enforces business invariants. Tests go in a separate .Tests project. Superseded in physical layout detail by ADR 0009.

documents.title: ADR 0009: Feature Slices Within Module Projects
documents.description: Authoritative physical layout for a module project: DomainModels/, Features/{Feature}CommandHandler, IXxxRepository at module root, Observability/, Services/, Extensions/, module registration. DTOs in Abstractions/DataTransferObjects/. Supersedes ADR 0007 for project-level structure.

documents.title: ADR 0010: Adopt OpenTelemetry for Comprehensive Observability
documents.description: Mandates OpenTelemetry for traces, metrics, and logs. Each module exposes an Observability/ folder with a custom ActivitySource and counters (e.g., ConferenceMetrics.cs). Wired through Aspire ServiceDefaults.

documents.title: ADR 0011: Centralized Frontend Styling Variables
documents.description: Requires all design tokens (colors, spacing, typography) to be declared as SASS/CSS variables in a single source file. Applies to Angular, React, Vue, and Blazor frontends.

documents.title: ADR 0012: Authentication with External Identity Providers
documents.description: Mandates OpenID Connect (OIDC) as the protocol for all external IdP integrations (Google, Microsoft Entra ID, Facebook). Covers JWT Bearer API auth, Microsoft.Identity.Web, refresh token strategy, PKCE for public clients, claims mapping, and a dedicated identity layer.

documents.title: ADR 0013: Authorization & Zero Trust Security Model
documents.description: Adopts Zero Trust principles (verify explicitly, least privilege, assume breach). Defines claims-based authorization with centrally registered policies, resource-based per-record access control, no implicit module trust, audit logging for sensitive operations, and strict JWT validation requirements.

documents.title: ADR 0014: Persistence Strategy and Repository Boundaries
documents.description: Defines module-owned persistence with EF Core confined to data adapter projects, aggregate-focused repositories, module-owned migrations, and schema-per-module as the default relational modular-monolith shape.

documents.title: ADR 0015: Resilience Strategy for Outbound Dependencies
documents.description: Standardizes Polly-based resilience policies at adapter boundaries only, including explicit timeouts, selective retries for transient failures, circuit breakers, and controlled fallback behavior.

documents.title: ADR 0016: Messaging and Integration-Event Delivery
documents.description: Defines when to use synchronous contracts versus integration events and requires outbox-driven publication plus idempotent consumers for durable cross-module workflows.

documents.title: ADR 0017: HTTP Error Contract and Problem Details
documents.description: Requires RFC 7807 Problem Details for API failures and standardizes how Result outcomes, validation errors, authorization failures, and unexpected exceptions map to HTTP responses.

documents.title: ADR 0018: Configuration and Options Binding
documents.description: Standardizes strongly typed options with startup validation, module-owned configuration sections, and externalized secret handling using bind-plus-validate patterns.

documents.title: Modular Monolith Architecture Design
documents.description: Architecture intent and trade-off guide for modular monoliths: boundary rules, in-process contract communication, consistency strategy, observability ownership, risks, and extraction path guidance.

documents.title: Pragmatic Domain-Driven Design Approach
documents.description: Practical DDD guidance for modular monoliths: when to use entities vs value objects, aggregate boundaries, domain events, bounded contexts, and how DDD concepts map to the module/feature-slice structure.

documents.title: API Idempotency for Commands
documents.description: Guidance for idempotent command endpoints using idempotency keys or business keys so retries do not duplicate externally visible side effects.

documents.title: API Versioning and Contract Evolution
documents.description: Recommends additive-first API evolution, deliberate deprecation, and consistent versioning only when backward compatibility cannot be preserved.

documents.title: Background Jobs and Hosted Services
documents.description: Guidance for BackgroundService and worker-style processing, including idempotency, cancellation, durable dispatch, retries at boundaries, and observability requirements.

documents.title: Blazor Frontend Framework Guidance
documents.description: Practical guidance for Blazor frontend setup, feature-based component structure, backend integration patterns, state management, caching strategy, and security recommendations.

documents.title: Caching Strategy
documents.description: Defines cache-aside as the default caching model, limits caching to read-oriented and externally derived data, and requires explicit TTL and invalidation ownership.

documents.title: C# Coding Style
documents.description: Prescribes C# coding conventions for .NET projects: file-scoped namespaces, sealed classes by default, nameof in exceptions, var usage, guard clauses, and modern C# features.

documents.title: Database Migration Workflow
documents.description: Defines a reviewable migration workflow with module-owned migrations, business-intent naming, explicit data-loss review, and no destructive production startup migrations.

documents.title: CI/CD Pipeline for Continuous Deployment
documents.description: Defines a production-grade CI/CD baseline for .NET services with required PR checks, automatic deployment from main, progressive rollout, post-deploy verification, and rollback readiness.

documents.title: Feature Flags and Rollout Safety
documents.description: Guidance for short-lived feature flags, rollout ownership, observability-backed releases, and avoiding flag sprawl or policy bypasses.

documents.title: Logging and Audit Logging
documents.description: Separates diagnostic logging from audit logging and defines the minimum fields, retention concerns, and redaction expectations for each.

documents.title: Object Calisthenics for Domain Code
documents.description: Applies the 9 Object Calisthenics rules to domain classes: one level of indentation, no else, wrap primitives, first-class collections, one dot per line, no abbreviations, small entities, two instance variables max, and no getters/setters.

documents.title: Specification Pattern for Business Rules
documents.description: Defines when to use the Specification pattern versus inline aggregate invariants: use for complex, reusable, or combinable rules; keep simple field checks inline.

documents.title: Architecture Testing for Layer and Module Boundaries
documents.description: Defines automated architecture tests for dependency direction, forbidden dependencies, and module boundary integrity using NetArchTest, including CI enforcement guidance.

documents.title: End-to-End Testing
documents.description: Defines Aspire-orchestrated E2E testing as black-box by nature, focused on critical business journeys and observable outcomes, with clear scope separation from integration tests.

documents.title: Integration Testing
documents.description: Defines integration testing as primarily gray-box with black-box assertions, allows module-specific projects for large solutions, recommends shared integration tests for cross-module and smaller solutions, and restricts mocking to external dependencies.

documents.title: Testing Shared Instructions
documents.description: Defines shared testing guidance across unit, integration, end-to-end, and architecture tests, including project layout, default test project structure, and CI execution order.

documents.title: Unit Testing with xUnit, Moq and Bogus
documents.description: Defines unit-test�specific practices including TDD workflow, test scope per class, parameterized tests, builder-first arrangement, assertion strategies, deterministic seeding, coverage targets, and over-mocking avoidance. Shared tooling and patterns are in Testing Shared Instructions.

documents.title: Validation Strategy
documents.description: Clarifies the split between boundary validation, application validation, and domain invariant enforcement, including FluentValidation-style boundary checks and consistent error reporting.

documents.title: Feature Slices Module Structure
documents.description: Copy-paste scaffold for a complete module: full folder tree (DomainModels/, Features/, Observability/, Services/, Extensions/), Abstractions project with DataTransferObjects/, Api project with Program.cs wiring, Data project, and Tests project with Moq/xUnit examples.

documents.title: Folder Structure Reference
documents.description: High-level solution folder map and navigation guide that points to detailed structure documents for module, feature-slice, and endpoint-specific layouts.

documents.title: Minimal API Endpoint Organization
documents.description: Template for organizing Minimal API endpoints within a module's .Api project: Endpoints/ folder, static MapXxxEndpoints extension methods, MapGroup with tags, and how endpoints delegate to ICommandHandler / IQueryHandler.

documents.title: Simple Solution Structure Design
documents.description: Visual blueprint of a non-modular single-solution profile: core/api/data projects without module folders. Aspire is optional; test topology is flexible with Unit plus optional Integration and/or E2E tests (or Unit only for very small solutions).

documents.title: GitHub Copilot Agent Configuration (github-app.yml)
documents.description: Standard configuration guideline for github-app.yml: mandatory pre-PR validation steps (restore, build, test), post-PR CI monitoring with auto-fix loop, review comment handling, PR conventions, and agent safety boundaries.

documents.title: MCP Server Configuration (.mcp.json)
documents.description: Standard .mcp.json setup for GitHub Copilot CLI, including required fields, baseline server entries for Microsoft Learn, JSdotNet Guidelines, and Aspire, plus maintenance best practices.

documents.title: ADR 0019: C# Standalone Script Files
documents.description: Adopts .NET 10 file-based apps (#: directives, dotnet run script.cs) as the standard for project automation scripts. Scripts are fully standalone .cs files in /scripts/ with no project file. NuGet packages declared via #:package align with Directory.Packages.props for version consistency. A scripts/Directory.Build.props isolates scripts from solution-level MSBuild settings.

documents.title: Style Guide: Overview
documents.description: Technology-agnostic UX style guide overview. Defines what is and isn't customizable per project, and maps to the five style guide documents (color, typography, spacing, motion, customization).

documents.title: Style Guide: Color Palette
documents.description: All color tokens for light and dark mode: brand, semantic, neutral/text, background, and border groups. Includes hex values, semantic names, usage rules, and contrast requirements. The only aspect projects may customize.

documents.title: Style Guide: Typography
documents.description: Fixed typography tokens: font families (Inter, Poppins, Fira Code), sizes (xsG��5xl), weights, line heights, and letter spacing. Includes default heading combinations and accessibility notes.

documents.title: Style Guide: Spacing and Layout
documents.description: Fixed spacing scale (4px base unit), layout grid, border radius, border width, shadows, and z-index scale. Covers usage rules for each token category.

documents.title: Style Guide: Motion and Interaction
documents.description: Fixed motion tokens: transition durations, easing curves, standard interaction patterns, focus state rules, reduced-motion guidance, and loading indicator patterns.

documents.title: Style Guide: Customization Guide
documents.description: Defines which color tokens may be overridden per project (brand and semantic only), the override contract (contrast requirements, both modes, documentation), the step-by-step process, and what happens if non-color tokens are overridden.
